$CRWV isn’t paying 15% interest. Only 4% of their debt costs that.

I went through the Q2 10-Q line by line. Out of ~$35B in debt, exactly one loan sits at 15%. It’s $1.3B, due March 2028, and already being paid down.

The 15% chart going around is the market yield on their 2032 bond. A higher yield doesn’t change what CoreWeave pays. It works like a mortgage. If you locked in at 3% and rates go to 7%, you’re still paying 3%. CoreWeave locked that bond at 9.625% and still pays 9.625%.

What they actually pay

> $6.6B of convertibles at ~2%
> ~$10B of bonds at 9-10%
> Most secured loans around 9%
> ~8.4% blended across everything

They have roughly $20B of 2026 capex left to fund, and 2027 will need more. Their main funding tool has been loans backed by customer contracts. The investment grade one backed by Meta priced around 5.9% in March. If they keep borrowing that way, I think the math holds.

Gartner says 80% of neocloud providers will stop operating independently by 2030 and I agree.

Sorry but not all of them will be winners, most of them will disappear even if demand is sky high.

If you read my longer takes you know that I think that as a category, neoclouds aren't a great business.

Capex drags on you every quarter, and the only way out is escape velocity: growing faster than your own spending. 

Meaning most will be acquired, merged or starved of capital.

In June Gartner forecasted neoclouds taking 20% of the AI cloud market by 2030. Fewer providers plus a bigger share means the survivors get much, much larger. 

Consolidation is how the winners get made.

So the real question is which one escapes, and here's why I think $NBIS is built differently:

+Customers fund the build. Prepayments covered 50–60% of the capex on its Q2 deals. Most neoclouds borrow against their GPUs, while Nebius gets its customers to pay up front.

+ The margins are already there: about 77% gross margin and a 41% adjusted EBITDA margin in Q2, on revenue up 454% year over year.

+ Pricing keeps rising. GPU prices went up another 17–21% on October 1, and new contracts are signing at $20–25M per MW.

+ It isn't drowning in interest. Last quarter $CRWV paid $640M of interest against $128M of adjusted operating income. Nebius's debt is mostly low-coupon convertibles.

+ The power is locked in. Contracted power has been raised three times this year, to 5 GW.

Gartner's real point is that the industry as a whole won't earn a 12% ROIC until 2032. An industry average tells you how the typical provider does, and I'm not betting on the typical provider. $NBIS is built different.

The risk with Nebius is financing, because the 5 GW build still needs about $250B.

So far they've done a stellar job handling it.

Macro comes and goes, but great companies endure.

$NBIS

I was thinking about what would actually make me sell my NBIS shares. 

Simplified, these are the five things that keep me honest, with how healthy each one looks today (1 = bad / 5= good):

+ Financing gets too expensive (3/5)
 NBIS still has to raise roughly $250B to build out its 5 GW, and only about 20% is secured. If converts and credit get much more expensive, or the market stops taking their paper, growth slows or the share count balloons.

+ Dilution outruns growth (4/5)
 Some dilution is the price of the build-out, and I'm fine with that. What would break the thesis is ARR per share stalling while the share count keeps climbing.

+ Pricing rolls over (5/5)
 The bull case leans on new contracts at $20–25M per MW and GPU prices that are still rising. If contract pricing or on-demand GPU prices start falling, the economics behind every gigawatt shrink.

+ Customers stop paying up front (4/5)
 Prepayments covering 50–60% of capex tell me customers can't find this capacity elsewhere. If those shrink, demand is cooling.

+ Power slips (3/5)
 Contracted power that doesn't come online on time is revenue that doesn't show up, and power is the slowest input in the whole stack.

Demand is the easy part right now. 

The weakest scores are on financing and delivery, and that's where I'll be watching.

This might be the most bullish memory chart I've seen all year.

Bloomberg Intelligence has HBM bit shipments going from about 5,000M GB in 2026 to roughly 18,000M GB by 2030, almost 4x in four years.

Over the same period, the average HBM price per GB more than doubles, from around $16 to about $35.

In memory, that almost never lasts for years. 

More supply has always meant lower prices, and that's what made this a cyclical business. Here volume and price climb together, which tells you demand is running ahead of everything the industry can build.

Only three companies in the world make HBM at scale, and $MU is one of them, with 26 strategic customer agreements already locking in demand through 2030.

More bits, at higher prices, with customers signed up for years. 

Mega bullish $MU.

$MU went from 16 to 26 strategic customer agreements in a single quarter, and now @elonmusk is calling Micron the reasonable one on future memory prices while its peers have been “extortionate.”

Those contracts now cover more than 35% of revenue through 2030, with about $150B in remaining performance obligations and $32B in customer commitments, mostly cash deposits. 

Customers are paying upfront to lock in memory supply years ahead, memory has never had visibility like this.

Every HBM bit takes 3 to 4 times the wafer capacity of standard DRAM, node migrations are slower and new cleanrooms take years. That keeps DRAM bit growth around the low 20s% through 2028, while AI capex, HBM content per accelerator and agentic workloads keep pushing demand higher.

The biggest knock on memory has always been the cycle. Boom, bust, repeat. Contracts like these are how you kill that argument, and Micron is clearly playing the long game here.

In the short term price follows sentiment, and sentiment on memory is awful right now. But in the long run price follows earnings, and these contracts lock in years of them.

Bullish $MU

越来越多 Crypto 交易所开始把业务重心往传统金融市场延伸。

其实对我这种同时交易美股和 Crypto 的人来说，需求一直很明确：能不能在同一个平台上完成更多资产的交易，减少账户和资金之间的切换成本？

所以最近看到 @Bybit 上线 Bybit Stocks ，我觉得还挺值得聊聊。

有几个地方值得关注：

1. Crypto 和美股之间的交易门槛正在降低

以前想配置美股，通常需要单独开通券商账户，资金也要在不同平台之间转来转去。
现在符合条件的用户可以直接通过 Bybit App 访问真实美股市场。

底层由 Infra Capital 提供券商服务，后台会为用户开设对应的券商账户，用户不需要额外管理一套独立的交易入口。

对于同时持有美股和 Crypto 的投资者来说，确实方便了不少。

注：Infra Capital Limited 是一家在毛里求斯注册、受当地金融监管机构监管的金融服务公司，也是 Bybit Stocks 的证券经纪合作方。
它的定位更接近 Introducing Broker（介绍经纪商）

2. 首批股票基本覆盖了目前市场的热门交易方向
首批包括 $NVDA、 $TSLA、 $BABA、  $SNDK、 $MU 等热门标的。

尤其是 $NVDA、 $MU、 $SNDK，本身就是我平时研究 AI CapEx、存储周期和期权流时经常关注的股票。

我觉得这批标的选择也挺有针对性，基本都是市场关注度和交易活跃度比较高的公司。

对于原本就在 Crypto 市场交易的用户，也多了一个接触传统美股的入口。

3. TradFi 和 Crypto 的融合正在加速
这也是我更关注的部分。

从美债 RWA、代币化股票，到现在直接通过 Crypto 交易所接入真实美股，传统金融资产进入 Crypto 生态的方式越来越丰富。

这里需要区分一下，Bybit Stocks 和平台上的 mStocks 是不同产品。

Bybit Stocks 接入的是传统证券市场，背后有实际的券商账户；mStocks 则属于独立的代币化产品。

长期来看，我认为 Crypto 交易所之间的竞争会逐渐向多资产交易延伸。

谁能提供更丰富的交易品种、更好的流动性和更低的跨市场使用门槛，谁就更有机会留住交易用户。

尤其是对于我们这种同时关注美股、Crypto 和宏观市场的人来说，未来跨市场交易可能会变得越来越方便。

【美股复盘 · 10月14日】

**大市**
AI与半导体链沽压主导全日，科网股成为重灾区，大市反复向下。纳指ETF（ $QQQ ）急泻1.97%，收报728.95点，失守730关；标普ETF（SPY ）跌1.08%，收报769.60点；罗素小型股ETF（IWM ）挫1.93%，收报271.37点。惟道指ETF（DIA ）在防守类与必需消费股支撑下靠稳，仅微跌0.11%，收报515.63点，表现一枝独秀。市宽极度偏弱，104只观察股中仅23只上升、81只下跌，跌股接近升股的四倍，显示沽压并非集中于个别重磅股，而是全面扩散。

**板块**
升幅榜由反向杠杆ETF包揽：三倍沽空半导体的 SOXS 暴升13.63%居首，三倍沽空纳指的 SQQQ 升5.93%，三倍沽空标普的 SPXU 升3.25%，印证资金对科技板块的对冲需求急增。防守类逆市造好——医药保险股联合健康（UNH ）升4.73%，制药股莫德纳（MRNA ）升4.65%、默沙东（MRK ）升3.80%、礼来（LLY ）升3.62%；国防股洛克希德马丁（LMT ）升3.61%；必需消费方面沃尔玛（WMT ）升3.46%、好市多（COST ）升2.87%。

跌方则清一色为AI叙事相关的高波幅板块。算力租赁及AI基建领跌：CoreWeave（CRWV ）重挫15.46%，IREN（IREN ）泻12.18%，Nebius（NBIS ）跌10.08%。光通讯及网络设备同遭洗仓：应用光电（AAOI ）跌11.82%，Ciena（CIEN ）跌10.19%，Credo（CRDO ）跌9.62%。量子计算概念亦被沽售，D-Wave（QBTS ）跌10.09%，IonQ（IONQ ）跌9.53%。硬件股戴尔（DELL ）跌11.27%，卫星通讯股AST SpaceMobile（ASTS ）跌10.46%。

**焦点**
消息面上，苹果就商业机密被窃一案起诉OpenAI，今日进入关键听证。市场留意的是诉讼本身的结构性代价：商业秘密案要胜诉，原告须先在诉状、证据披露程序中把「秘密」描述清楚，部分内容最终或进入公开卷宗——嘴最严的公司，为护住一件未发布的产品，选择了一个必须先把它说出来的场合。另一边，OpenAI指控苹果挖角并带走文件，苹果的回应是已按对方指认的「那一份文件」全面检索，在任何苹果系统上均未发现。值得注意的是，OpenAI能事后精确点名是哪一份文档，意味其内部对每一次文件访问皆有留痕，细至单一文件、单一人员、单一时点。此为事件层面观察，与今日个股波幅无直接因果。

**小结**
全日走势呈现清晰的板块轮替而非单纯恐慌：资金自高估值AI链（算力、光通讯、量子）撤出，转入医药、国防与必需消费等现金流确定的防守阵地，道指与纳指表现的巨大落差即为此一轮动的最直接读数。分析指，纳指ETF失守730关为短线转弱讯号，而标普ETF 770关为后市首个须收复的关键位；在市宽未见改善、升跌比仍悬殊之前，反弹宜视为沽压中的喘息而非趋势反转。
